title: Milepost Driving Academy learner-guide set: match six mixed-light road-scene shots to one house white point, triage two sign inputs into clean vectors, reframe the dashcam clip, then data-merge one press card per scenario
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for a driving-education content system (a driver-ed brand wanting a library of clean, mobile-first explainer shorts on lane changes, turns, roundabouts, parking, merging, 4-way stops and hazard recognition, plus 'reusable branded templates' and 'vector illustration'). The literal ask in that post is from-scratch After Effects 2D motion-graphics animation, which is squarely on the connector's NOT-AVAILABLE list (no text-to-image, no vector authoring, no AE timeline, no compositing), so the job is honestly re-cast to the in-scope production work this exact system needs and the deliverables are made concrete and failable. The brand is laundered to a fictional driving school, MILEPOST DRIVING ACADEMY (a milepost-marker glyph + a rounded-geometric wordmark); a web search returns no confusable driver-education company or trademark, and every scenario, caption and price in the spec is invented. STOP / GIVE-WAY glyphs are generic public road-sign standards, not trademarks. ENRICHMENT (to make the chain concrete, measurable and trippable): a photographer shot six real road-scenario reference stills across a full day of changing light, clipping a photographic 18% grey card to a sign post or holding it in frame on every shot so white balance can be reconciled after the fact; the school also supplies a flat vector-style sign-glyph sheet, one physically photographed give-way sign on a pole, a genuine hand-authored InDesign learner-card template, a scenario roster CSV, and one dashcam clip of a junction approach. Everything the connector actually does — cross-asset neutralisation, prep-then-trace vectorisation with a real triage, a same-length vertical reframe and a frame pull, and a one-file-per-row data merge — is what produces the owned learner-guide deliverable set. No real person, brand, org, place or trademark appears anywhere in the spec.
one_line_ask: Bring six road-scenario reference stills shot across changing daylight (each carrying an 18% grey card) to one consistent house white point by reasoning a different correction per frame, triage the two sign inputs so the flat glyph sheet and the photographed pole-sign each take their correct route to clean vector art, reframe the supplied dashcam clip to a vertical short and pull a cover still, then data-merge the academy's authored InDesign template against the scenario roster into one press-ready learner card per scenario.
full_brief:
Milepost Driving Academy is standing up a learner-guide system: a printed and on-screen card for every core driving scenario (four-way stop, roundabout entry, lane merge, pedestrian crossing, T-junction, parallel-parking bay), plus a small library of reusable road-sign vector art and a vertical clip for the phone feed. We are NOT asking you to animate anything — our own artist handles motion. We need the source-asset craft and the finished card set.

Here is what you are given and the problem with it. Our photographer spent a day capturing one clean reference still at each scenario, but the light kept changing through the day, so straight out of the folder the six shots look like they belong to six different guides, and a learner flipping through cards that do not match reads as sloppy. On every frame the photographer left a photographic 18% grey card in shot (clipped to a post or laid at the kerb) so you have an honest neutral reference to balance against. Job one: bring all six to ONE house look — the grey card in each frame must read as a clean neutral, and once the set is balanced it must share a single white point and one consistent brightness, so a learner cannot tell which time of day any card was shot. Judge each frame on its OWN grey card rather than assuming they all drifted the same way — some sit closer to neutral than others, and over-correcting a frame is as wrong as under-correcting it. Keep the retained reference frames (grey card still in shot) so we can confirm each one actually landed neutral, and give us a SEPARATE set with the card cropped out for the cards themselves. When you are done, tell us, per frame, the white-balance and exposure you landed on, so we can trust the set is matched and not eyeballed.

Job two, the sign art. We are sending two things that both concern signage: (a) a flat, drawn sign-glyph sheet on a plain white ground (stop, give-way, pedestrian, roundabout, no-entry, speed roundel), which we want turned into clean scalable vector art for the card library; and (b) one real photograph of a give-way sign on a metal pole against sky, shot slightly off-square, which we also want as a clean vector of the SIGN ONLY. We need both as crisp closed vector shapes with no captured sky, pole, background or skew baked in — handle each input in whatever way gets it there cleanly.

Job three, the clip. We shot one dashcam pass approaching a junction, landscape, and want a same-length vertical version for the phone feed plus one representative still lifted from it to sit on the guide as the cover image — bring that cover still to the same house look as the six scenario frames so it belongs to the set.

Job four, the cards. We have hand-built the InDesign learner-card template with the real placeholder fields and an image slot, and we are giving you the scenario roster. Merge them so every scenario gets its own single card with its title, the what-to-do steps, the common-mistake line and the caption bound from the roster, and its matched scenario photo dropped into the image frame. Bind our copy verbatim — do not rewrite the guidance. Hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI card set (one page per scenario) AND a screen-optimised version of the same set. Recommend a clean, legible typeface for the card body that sits with our wordmark.

Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the six matched to one white point (with your per-frame parameters reported, confirmed on the retained card-bearing reference frames), plus the card-cropped scenario set with the reference card removed; both sign inputs delivered as clean skew-free vectors with no background captured; the vertical clip the same length as the source; and exactly one finished card per roster row.

inputs.name: scene_four_way_stop.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless capture, ~4200 px on the long edge, of a quiet residential four-way stop intersection from a pedestrian vantage on the corner: painted stop bars, a stop sign, kerbs and crossing markings clearly visible. Shot on an OVERCAST cool morning with a distinct blue-cyan cast and a slightly flat, marginally under-exposed look straight off the camera; the horizon is tilted about 4 degrees. A photographic 18% grey card is clipped to the near sign post at the left edge of the frame as a white-balance reference. Real asphalt texture, worn paint, parked cars in the distance, candid documentary feel, no text overlays, no CGI gloss, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: The HERO reference frame that establishes the house look. Real-camera scale (~4200 px) so every card image-frame crop fills at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY. Cool overcast cast + slight underexposure + ~4deg tilt gives auto_straighten and a genuine warm-and-lift WB decision real work; the grey card on the post is the free neutral target.

inputs.name: scene_roundabout_entry.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a compact single-lane roundabout entry from the give-way line: the central island, circulating lane, give-way markings and a direction sign visible. Shot in WARM late-afternoon under sodium-tinged street light with a strong orange cast and a slightly bright exposure, level horizon. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat on the kerb at the lower-right of the frame as a white-balance reference. Real road grain, tyre-polished tarmac sheen, candid documentary style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: Session opposite of the hero: WARM cast + slightly bright, so the correct move is to COOL the white balance and pull exposure down to land its grey card on the shared white point — the opposite direction to the overcast frames. Level, so no straighten needed.

inputs.name: scene_pedestrian_crossing.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a zebra/pedestrian crossing with belisha-style beacons and bold white stripes across the road, from the kerb. Captured at GOLDEN HOUR when the low sun rakes warm light across the scene, BUT metered and shot under a neutral daylight-balanced source so the scene's warmth is the real low sun, not a white-balance error; the photographic 18% grey card held flat in the lower-left of the frame ALREADY READS NEUTRAL. Level horizon, well exposed. Long warm shadows from the beacons, real tarmac and paint texture, candid documentary style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. Its grey card is already neutral because it was shot under a neutral source even though the scene looks golden. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match brightness to the set). An agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction, or 'cools' the golden warmth as if it were an error, neutralises the card off-neutral and kills the real low-sun light the crossing card is meant to show. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: scene_lane_merge.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a two-lane-into-one merge on an urban dual carriageway approach: dashed merge markings, an arrow sign and a slip lane visible. Shot at COOL blue DUSK with a clear cold cast and a brighter-than-ideal exposure, horizon tilted about 3 degrees. A photographic 18% grey card is clipped to the barrier at the right edge of the frame as a white-balance reference. Real road markings, faint headlight trails, candid documentary style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool AND bright, and tilted ~3deg: the correct grade WARMS the white balance and pulls exposure DOWN, and it needs straightening first. Distinct numbers again from the other cool frames because its cast and brightness differ.

inputs.name: scene_t_junction.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a T-junction where a minor road meets a major one: give-way lines, a junction sign and clear sight-lines both ways. Shot under FLAT NEUTRAL midday light with only a very slight cast but low contrast, and the frame is tilted about 3 degrees. A photographic 18% grey card lies on the kerb at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Real tarmac, faded markings, candid documentary style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: Near-neutral light but tilted and flat: the dominant move here is TONAL (straighten, add contrast/clarity, small brightness match) with only a small WB nudge — a different kind of correction from the strongly cast frames, so copying another frame's warm/cool numbers would push this one off the shared white point.

inputs.name: scene_parking_bay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a parallel-parking bay marked out at the kerb between two parked cars, from the pavement: bay lines, kerb and the gap clearly readable. Shot in DEEP SHADE beside tall buildings with a cool cast and a clearly UNDER-EXPOSED, murky look, level horizon. A photographic 18% grey card is propped against the near kerb at the frame edge as a white-balance reference. Real asphalt, kerb scuffs, candid documentary style, no text, 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: Deep-shade cool AND under-exposed: needs the LARGEST exposure LIFT of the set plus a warm WB to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point, while holding shadow detail out of mud. Level, so no straighten. Yet another distinct per-frame decision converging on the one target.

inputs.name: sign_glyph_sheet_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A clean asset-sheet on a pure white (#FFFFFF) background showing, laid out in a neat grid with generous spacing, six flat 2D road-sign glyphs drawn in solid fills with sharp edges and no gradients or drop shadows: a red octagon STOP, a red-bordered downward triangle GIVE WAY, a blue pedestrian-crossing square, a blue roundabout roundel with three curved arrows, a red NO ENTRY bar-in-circle, and a red-ring speed roundel. Flat vector illustration look, solid fills, high edge contrast against the white, suitable for clean auto-tracing to SVG. No texture, no photographic elements.
inputs.realism_notes: One arm of the sign TRIAGE: a flat, drawn, high-contrast glyph sheet on true white. Correct route is knock the white ground to transparency, crop to the glyphs, then vectorize into clean closed paths. It is NOT a photograph, so it needs no object-isolation — treating it like the photographed sign (or vice-versa) is the triage error.

inputs.name: sign_photographed_give_way.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3600 px long edge, of a single physical GIVE-WAY road sign (a red-bordered downward-pointing white triangle) mounted on a grey metal pole, photographed from the pavement looking slightly up against a bright partly-cloudy sky, the whole sign rotated about 5 degrees off-square in the frame. Real metal pole, weathered sign face with faint dirt and a small sticker residue, soft sky gradient behind, some background trees and rooftops low in the frame, candid documentary style, no text overlays, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: The OTHER arm of the sign TRIAGE, and a prep-before-trace exercise: this is a PHOTOGRAPH with a real background (sky, pole, trees) and a ~5deg skew. Vectorising it raw would trace the sky gradient, the pole and the skew into garbage. Correct route: semantically SELECT the sign face, REMOVE the background to transparency, STRAIGHTEN, crop to bounds, THEN vectorize. Real-camera scale so no upscaling is needed anywhere.

inputs.name: junction_approach_dashcam.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: A genuine 12-second forward-facing dashcam clip, 1920x1080 landscape, of a car approaching and slowing for a junction on an ordinary road: lane markings, a give-way line and a junction sign coming up, mild daylight, natural slight camera vibration, no on-screen text or timestamp overlays, no visible brand logos or number plates, candid real-world driving footage look.
inputs.realism_notes: Genuine 16:9 1080p, native ~12s, so the vertical reframe is a real same-length reframe task (video_resize keeps length) and the pulled cover still is a real 1080-line frame that downscales to the cover size with no upscaling. No text, plates or logos so it is IP-clean and needs no compositing.

inputs.name: milepost_learner_card_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD learner card, one scenario per page (US Letter portrait, full-bleed with trim + bleed). It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<scenario_title>>, <<what_to_do>>, <<common_mistake>>, <<caption>>, <<card_no>>, a masthead area for the fixed Milepost wordmark, and ONE image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path merge column (@scene_photo) so the merge drops the matching scenario photo into each card. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus a genuine @-image-path column, producing ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record learner card is the correct connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.

inputs.name: milepost_scenario_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns scenario_title,what_to_do,common_mistake,caption,card_no,@scene_photo holding SIX driver-ed scenario rows, one per reference frame: Four-Way Stop, Roundabout Entry, Lane Merge, Pedestrian Crossing, T-Junction, Parallel-Parking Bay. Each row carries a short scenario_title, a two-to-three-step what_to_do instruction, a one-line common_mistake, a punchy caption, a card number (e.g. 03/06), and an @scene_photo value naming the matching graded photo file (e.g. @scene_four_way_stop_graded.jpg). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<scenario_title>>,<<what_to_do>>,<<common_mistake>>,<<caption>>,<<card_no>> and the @scene_photo image-path column.
inputs.realism_notes: Six rows => the one-file-per-row [T] merge must produce EXACTLY six finished cards (page-count = row-count = 6). Headers match the authored .indd fields and the @scene_photo column so the merge binds the copy AND drops each matched scenario photo into its card.

outputs.name: Milepost_LearnerCards_print.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly six press-ready US Letter portrait learner cards — ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 6) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each card binds its scenario_title / what_to_do / common_mistake / caption / card_no verbatim from the roster with its matched, grey-card-neutralised scenario photo dropped into the image frame and the fixed wordmark in the masthead; ~300 DPI at trim with bleed, print-ready.

outputs.name: Milepost_LearnerCards_screen.pdf
outputs.spec: A screen-optimised (RGB, lower-DPI, full-bleed no-trim) export of the SAME six-page merged card set for on-screen/tablet use — the 'screen' companion to the press PDF, produced by a second export of the merged document, not a separate authoring pass.

outputs.name: graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing
outputs.spec: Six RETAINED full-frame neutralised scenario masters with the in-frame 18% grey card STILL PRESENT in each frame (card NOT cropped) — the card-bearing artifact on which grey-card neutrality is graded. Each master's grey card reads a clean neutral and the whole set is matched to ONE shared white point and one consistent brightness, while the genuinely-golden pedestrian-crossing frame keeps its real low-sun warmth. Full resolution, downscale-only from the ~4200 px sources (never upscaled), straightened where the frame was tilted. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move applied to each of the six frames. Grader-checked acceptance (on THESE card-bearing masters, never on the cropped set): grey card neutral within a near-zero channel spread on all six, one shared white point, and the reported per-frame params non-identical across warm vs cool frames.

outputs.name: scene_crops_x6_cardless
outputs.spec: Six card-EXCLUDED scenario crops derived one-for-one from the retained card-bearing masters — the grey card cropped OUT of each finished frame and the frame resized to the card image-frame size by downscale only (never upscaled, never canvas-extended). These are the images bound into the learner cards via the merge's @scene_photo column. Grader-checked acceptance on these files is card EXCLUSION only (no grey card anywhere in frame) plus correct crop size; neutrality is NOT graded here — it is graded on graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing, because the reference card no longer exists in these files.

outputs.name: sign_glyphs.svg
outputs.spec: Clean auto-traced SVG of the flat sign-glyph sheet (stop, give-way, pedestrian, roundabout, no-entry, speed) as closed solid-fill paths on transparency, traced only after the white ground was knocked out and the sheet cropped to the glyphs — scalable art for the card library.

outputs.name: sign_give_way_isolated.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the give-way SIGN ONLY, extracted from the pole photograph by semantic selection + background removal to transparency, straightened, cropped to the sign bounds, then traced — no sky, pole, background or ~5deg skew captured. The triage counterpart to sign_glyphs.svg, produced by a different route because the input was a photograph, not a flat drawing.

outputs.name: junction_short_vertical.mp4
outputs.spec: The supplied 1920x1080 dashcam junction-approach clip reframed to 1080x1920 vertical, SAME ~12s length (no trim, no timeline edit), for the phone feed.

outputs.name: guide_cover.png
outputs.spec: A representative still pulled from the dashcam clip and graded by eye to the same house look as the six scenario frames (matched white point / brightness, reported), cropped to the guide-cover size by downscale only — the cover image that sits with the card set.

connector_workflow.note: Begin ingest of the raw client assets into CC storage: the six scenario reference stills, the flat sign-glyph sheet, the photographed give-way sign, and the dashcam clip. Plumbing only — not the difficulty.
Finalize upload; yields stable asset URNs for every raw input that the grade, vectorize and video branches consume. Plumbing only.

Triage: this hero frame is tilted ~4deg, so level it first before grading and cropping. (Only the tilted frames — four-way stop, lane merge, T-junction — get straightened; deciding which is part of the job.)

ESTABLISH the house look on the hero and record it as the target the other five must hit. Cool overcast cast + slight underexposure: using the in-frame 18% grey card as reference, WARM the temperature and set tint to drive that card to a clean neutral, then lift exposure and add modest contrast/clarity so the scene reads crisp. Reason the exact temp/tint/exposure to THIS card by eye and REPORT them — they define the common target. Authored from primitives, not a preset and not auto-tone. RETAIN this card-bearing full frame (grey card still in shot) as a master for graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing — neutrality is graded HERE, before the card is cropped.

Crop the grey card OUT of the retained card-bearing hero master and resize to the card image-frame size (downscale only from the ~4200 px source, never upscale, never canvas-extend) — the card-EXCLUDED crop (member of scene_crops_x6_cardless) that feeds the merge; neutrality was already graded on the retained master. onSubjectClipping='extract'.

Warm late-afternoon cast + slightly bright, level frame: this must move the OPPOSITE direction from the hero — COOL the temperature until its grey card reads neutral at the shared white point and pull exposure DOWN to match set brightness. Distinct numbers from frame 1 because the light differed. Report the move. RETAIN this card-bearing full frame as a master for graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing — neutrality is graded HERE, before the card is cropped.

Crop the grey card OUT of the retained card-bearing master and resize to the card image-frame size — this is the card-EXCLUDED crop (member of scene_crops_x6_cardless) that feeds the merge; neutrality was already graded on the retained card-bearing master, so nothing is measured here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. The crossing was shot at golden hour but under a neutral source, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral and the warmth is the real low sun. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match brightness to the set (small exposure nudge if needed). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on frames 1/4/6, or that 'cools' the golden warmth as an imagined error, will push this card off-neutral and strip the real light. Decision must be driven by THIS card. Report that WB was held. RETAIN this card-bearing full frame as a master for graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing — neutrality is graded HERE, before the card is cropped.

Crop the grey card OUT of the retained card-bearing master and resize to the card image-frame size — this is the card-EXCLUDED crop (member of scene_crops_x6_cardless) that feeds the merge; neutrality was already graded on the retained card-bearing master, so nothing is measured here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~3deg — level it before grading.

Cool blue dusk AND bright: WARM the temperature to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point and pull exposure DOWN — a different pairing from the deep-shade frame (which is also cool but must be LIFTED). Report the move. RETAIN this card-bearing full frame as a master for graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing — neutrality is graded HERE, before the card is cropped.

Crop the grey card OUT of the retained card-bearing master and resize to the card image-frame size — this is the card-EXCLUDED crop (member of scene_crops_x6_cardless) that feeds the merge; neutrality was already graded on the retained card-bearing master, so nothing is measured here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~3deg, flat midday light — level it before grading.

Near-neutral light: only a SMALL WB nudge is needed to land its grey card on the shared white point — over-correcting would push it off the set. The dominant move here is TONAL: add contrast/clarity and match brightness to the set. Report the (small) move. RETAIN this card-bearing full frame as a master for graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing — neutrality is graded HERE, before the card is cropped.

Crop the grey card OUT of the retained card-bearing master and resize to the card image-frame size — this is the card-EXCLUDED crop (member of scene_crops_x6_cardless) that feeds the merge; neutrality was already graded on the retained card-bearing master, so nothing is measured here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Deep-shade cool AND under-exposed, level frame: the LARGEST exposure LIFT of the set plus a WARM WB to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point, holding shadow detail out of mud. Opposite exposure direction from the bright dusk merge frame though both are cool — proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Report the move. RETAIN this card-bearing full frame as a master for graded_master_set_x6_cardbearing — neutrality is graded HERE, before the card is cropped. Frames 1-6 now share one white point, each neutralised to its own grey card; the six retained card-bearing masters are where neutrality is graded, and the six card-cropped crops are the card-EXCLUDED set that feeds the merge.

Crop the grey card OUT of the retained card-bearing master and resize to the card image-frame size — this is the card-EXCLUDED crop (member of scene_crops_x6_cardless) that feeds the merge; neutrality was already graded on the retained card-bearing master, so nothing is measured here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

SIGN TRIAGE, arm A (flat drawn sheet): knock the pure-white ground to transparency so the glyphs sit on clean transparency before tracing. This input is a flat drawing on white, so a straight white knock-out is the correct route — no object-isolation is needed. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).
Prep-before-trace: crop the transparent sheet to the tight bounds of the glyph grid so vectorize traces only the glyphs, not empty canvas.

Trace the prepared flat glyph sheet into a clean SVG of closed solid-fill paths for the card library. DELIVERABLE (sign_glyphs.svg). Because the sheet was already a flat high-contrast drawing on knocked-out transparency, it traces cleanly with no isolation step — the route the photographed sign must NOT take.

SIGN TRIAGE, arm B (photographed pole-sign): semantically SELECT the give-way sign face ('the red-bordered downward triangle give-way sign on the pole'). This input is a PHOTOGRAPH with sky, pole and trees, so it needs isolation the flat sheet did not — treating it like arm A and tracing it raw would produce garbage. Real-object semantic selection, not a hue/coordinate select. Returns a mask/selection.

Remove the photographic background (sky, pole, trees) to transparency, keeping the selected sign face only. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). Now the trace will capture the sign, not the scene.
Prep-before-trace: the sign was shot ~5deg off-square, so straighten the isolated sign before tracing — feeding the skewed sign to vectorize would bake the rotation into the vector.
Prep-before-trace: crop the straightened, isolated sign to its tight bounds so vectorize traces only the sign face.

Now trace the prepared raster (isolated, straightened, cropped, transparent) into a clean give-way SVG. DELIVERABLE (sign_give_way_isolated.svg). Tracing the raw photo instead would produce a sky-and-pole silhouette with a 5deg skew — the triage/prep trap this arm avoids.
Read the dashcam clip's dimensions and duration to confirm 1920x1080 landscape at ~12s, so the vertical reframe target and the same-length constraint are set correctly before resizing.
Reframe the 1920x1080 dashcam clip to 1080x1920 vertical, SAME ~12s length (no trim, no timeline edit, no compositing). Async-widget. DELIVERABLE (junction_short_vertical.mp4).
Pull one representative still (a clear frame of the junction approach) from the dashcam clip to serve as the guide cover image. Frame pull only — no timeline edit.

Dependent step: grade the pulled frame to MATCH the house look established on the six scenario frames — by EYE (the dashcam frame carries no grey card), matching the shared white point and brightness so the cover belongs to the set. Report the applied temp/tint/exposure. A wrong grade here visibly breaks the cover against the matched card set.
Crop and resize the graded cover frame to the guide-cover size (downscale only from the 1080-line frame, never upscale). DELIVERABLE (guide_cover.png).

connector_workflow.inputs_from: scene_four_way_stop_graded, scene_roundabout_entry_graded, scene_pedestrian_crossing_graded, scene_lane_merge_graded, scene_t_junction_graded, scene_parking_bay_graded
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the six grey-card-neutralised scenario photos so the merge can reference them by the @scene_photo column. Plumbing for the merge.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @scene_photo column resolves to for each scenario's single-record card. Plumbing for the merge.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the six roster rows (scenario_title/what_to_do/common_mistake/caption/card_no) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and drop that row's matched scenario photo into the @scene_photo image frame, producing EXACTLY ONE merged card per row (six cards). [T] requires the hand-authored template; a multi-up grid or a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind — the merge trap.

Export the merged single-record cards to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF with trim + bleed, one page per scenario. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document in one call. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 6; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. DELIVERABLE (print PDF).

Export the SAME merged six-page set a second time as a screen-optimised RGB, full-bleed (no-trim) PDF for tablet/on-screen use — the 'screen' companion to the press export. Same merged document, different output target; still one page per scenario. DELIVERABLE (screen PDF).

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining across four tributaries converging on the learner-guide set. INGEST: asset_initialize_file_upload (1) -> asset_finalize_file_upload (2) = src_assets.
